html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Complete Install And Startup Manual

This manual starts after the SMTO source has already been synced or cloned onto the machine. It ends with a usable local agent system: Dockerized SMTO services, a reachable gateway, an attached LLM endpoint, and a first validated Agent UI request.

Docker is the preferred application path. It builds and runs the Agent runtime, Agent UI, manual, website, and audio runtime from the repository scripts. The gateway and LLM server remain separate because they are machine-facing infrastructure: gateways touch shells and terminals, and LLM servers own GPUs, model weights, and inference processes.

The Required Order

Bring the system up in this order:

  1. Build and run Docker services.
  2. Install and run at least one gateway.
  3. Attach an existing OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint or create a vllm conda environment and launch a local model.
  4. Validate every layer with health checks.
  5. Open the Agent UI and run a read-only request.

The gateway step is crucial. The gateway is the "hands" of SMTO. The Agent runtime can reason, validate, ask for approval, and prepare command capsules, but gateway processes are what actually run shell commands on the machines you control. Without a reachable gateway, the UI can load and the LLM can answer some direct questions, but command-backed agent work cannot operate properly.

flowchart TD A[Source synced down] --> B[Build Docker image] B --> C[Start all Docker services] C --> D[Install gateway on each execution machine] D --> E[Start gateway and verify /healthz] E --> F{LLM path} F -->|Existing endpoint| G[Configure OpenAI-compatible /v1 base URL] F -->|Local vLLM| H[Create conda env and run src/llm launcher] G --> I[Verify /v1/models] H --> I I --> J[Open Agent UI] J --> K[Run read-only request]

What You Are Installing

Component Default URL Installed by Purpose

Audio runtime Docker-internal http://audio:8012 Docker all-services stack Voice transcription support
Manual service http://127.0.0.1:8013/manual Docker all-services stack Searchable product and architecture manual
Website service http://127.0.0.1:8014/website Docker all-services stack Product website and manual entry points

LLM server http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 by default Existing server or vLLM script OpenAI-compatible model endpoint

Prerequisites

Install or confirm these before starting:

  • Git, with the repository already synced down.
  • Docker Engine with Compose v2.
  • curl for health checks.
  • Python 3.11 or newer for native gateway setup.
  • Conda or Miniconda only if you want the local vLLM setup path.
  • A reachable OpenAI-compatible model endpoint, or GPU hardware suitable for the local vLLM model you choose.
  • Network access between the Agent runtime container and each gateway or LLM host.

On Linux, the all-services compose file uses host.docker.internal via a host gateway entry so the container can call a gateway running on the Docker host. On Docker Desktop or remote gateway deployments, use the gateway's reachable host or LAN IP when loopback does not mean the same machine.

Step 1: Confirm Repository Root

From the repository root, confirm the expected scripts are present:

pwd
ls docker-all-services docker src src/llm src/gateway_agent

You should see:

  • docker-all-services/build.sh
  • docker-all-services/start.sh
  • src/gateway_agent/install.sh
  • src/gateway_agent/startup.sh
  • src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

Step 2: Build Docker

Build the preferred all-services image:

./docker-all-services/build.sh

To tag a specific image version:

./docker-all-services/build.sh v1.0.0

The all-services build uses docker/server.Dockerfile and creates an image named smto-all-services:latest unless SMTO_IMAGE or SMTO_VERSION is set.

Step 3: Run Docker

Start the full local product stack:

./docker-all-services/start.sh

Run in the background:

./docker-all-services/start.sh -d

Start a tagged version:

./docker-all-services/start.sh v1.0.0

Open:

Service URL
Agent UI http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui
Runtime health http://127.0.0.1:8011/healthz
Manual http://127.0.0.1:8013/manual
Manual health http://127.0.0.1:8013/healthz
Website http://127.0.0.1:8014/website

Watch logs:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs -f

Stop the stack without deleting persisted state:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml down

Step 4: Install The Gateway

Install the gateway on every machine that should execute commands. For the Docker host:

./src/gateway_agent/install.sh

This creates src/gateway_agent/.venv and installs the gateway runtime with the Python tooling expected by the agent.

Start the local loopback gateway:

./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh

Verify it:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/capabilities

The default gateway identity is:

GATEWAY_NODE_NAME=localhost
GATEWAY_BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1
GATEWAY_BIND_PORT=8787

For a gateway on a different trusted machine, choose a unique node name and bind to a reachable interface:

GATEWAY_NODE_NAME=workstation ./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8787

Then add that gateway from the Agent UI Gateway drawer with a nickname, host or IP, port, and node. The gateway does not include built-in authentication, so do not expose it to an untrusted network. Use loopback, a firewall, a VPN, or a trusted reverse proxy.

flowchart LR User[User] --> UI[Agent UI] UI --> Runtime[Agent runtime] Runtime --> Registry[Gateway registry] Registry --> G1[Gateway A\nlocalhost\nLinux workstation] Registry --> G2[Gateway B\nbuild-node\nLinux server] Registry --> G3[Gateway C\nmacbook\nmacOS laptop] G1 --> S1[Shell, terminal, workspace] G2 --> S2[Shell, terminal, workspace] G3 --> S3[Shell, terminal, workspace]

Step 5: Attach An Existing LLM Endpoint

SMTO expects an OpenAI-compatible API. The endpoint must support:

  • GET /v1/models
  • POST /v1/chat/completions

The default local endpoint is:

http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1

Verify an existing endpoint:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

In the Agent UI, open Settings, then LLM Endpoint, and set:

Field Example
Scheme http
Host / IP 127.0.0.1
Port 8000
Base path /v1
Model auto or an explicit served model id

Use auto when /v1/models returns a reliable model list. Use an explicit model id when the model server requires it.

Step 6: Or Create A Local vLLM Conda Environment

Use this path when you want to host the model yourself. The current official vLLM quickstart recommends Python 3.12 and supports installing vLLM through uv inside a conda environment. Upstream references: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/quickstart/ and https://vllm.ai/releases.

conda create -n vllm python=3.12 -y
conda activate vllm
pip install --upgrade uv
uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto

Then launch one of the repository's vLLM profiles:

./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

For a smaller first test:

./src/llm/start-qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct.sh

Useful overrides:

PORT=8001 MAX_MODEL_LEN=16384 ./src/llm/start-qwen2.5-coder-32b-awq.sh
GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.86 ./src/llm/start-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh
MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 ./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

If a model fails with GPU memory pressure, reduce MAX_MODEL_LEN first, then reduce GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION, then choose a smaller model profile.

The Agent UI Settings drawer can also ask the gateway to start and stop the configured local LLM command. That path uses these gateway-backed routes:

  • GET /api/agent/llm/status
  • GET /api/agent/llm/log
  • POST /api/agent/llm/start
  • POST /api/agent/llm/stop

The gateway must be running before those LLM launch controls can work.

flowchart TD Runtime[Agent runtime] --> Choice{LLM endpoint} Choice --> Existing[Existing OpenAI-compatible server] Choice --> Local[Local vLLM launched from conda env] Local --> Conda[conda env: vllm] Conda --> Script[src/llm/start-*.sh] Existing --> API[/v1/models and /v1/chat/completions] Script --> API API --> Runtime

Step 7: Validate Every Layer

Run these checks from the host:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8011/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8013/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8014/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

If Docker is running the all-services stack, also verify gateway and model reachability from the server container:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/healthz
docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'
sequenceDiagram participant User participant Docker as Docker services participant Gateway participant LLM participant UI as Agent UI User->>Docker: ./docker-all-services/start.sh User->>Gateway: ./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh User->>LLM: Start existing endpoint or vLLM script User->>Docker: curl /healthz User->>Gateway: curl /healthz User->>LLM: curl /v1/models User->>UI: Submit read-only prompt UI->>Gateway: Validated read-only command UI->>LLM: Structured model calls UI-->>User: Response with command evidence

Step 8: First Agent UI Request

Open:

http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui

Try a read-only request:

What repository workspace can you see, what branch is checked out, and which gateway handled the shell command?

Expected behavior:

  • The model helps classify and plan the request.
  • The runtime validates the action contract and shell safety.
  • The gateway runs the read-only command.
  • The response shows command evidence and a final summary.
  • Mutating commands pause for approval before execution.

Manual And Native Source Alternatives

Docker is preferred for running the product stack, but the native source path is still useful for development:

./install.sh
./startup.sh

Start only the manual:

./setup-manual.sh
./startmanual.sh --reload

Native runtime ports:

Service URL
Agent UI https://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui when SSL is enabled; http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui otherwise
Audio runtime http://127.0.0.1:8012/healthz
Manual service http://127.0.0.1:8013/manual

startup.sh accepts:

./startup.sh --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8011 --audio-port 8012 --manual-port 8013
./startup.sh --https
./startup.sh --reload

Skip optional child services when needed:

AOR_AUDIO_TRANSCRIBER_AUTOSTART=0 ./startup.sh
AOR_MANUAL_AUTOSTART=0 ./startup.sh

Troubleshooting

If Docker services do not start:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml ps
docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs -f

If the Agent UI opens but command execution fails, check the gateway first:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/capabilities

If the Docker server cannot reach a host gateway, verify the host gateway name:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/healthz

If model calls fail, verify the exact /v1 URL and bearer key:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

If vLLM cannot load the selected model, start with a smaller profile or reduce context:

MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 ./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

If ports are busy, change the compose environment or use the native launcher port flags. The all-services defaults are 8011 for the Agent runtime, 8013 for the manual, 8014 for the website, 8787 for the gateway, and 8000 for the LLM endpoint.
